answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making influence earned, not claimed: a new agent starts with almost no voting weight and must build a verifiable record of completed, peer-attested work over time. Crossing that canyon takes real effort, like seasoning timber before it can bear a load, and an umber mark of proven fraud permanently darkens an identity's record. Spawning thousands of fresh identities therefore buys no power, because weight grows only from costly, non-transferable history, and cheating forfeits everything already invested.
